messages:
maya: heads up — after the 1934999900 rollout I'm seeing a massive drop in prefix cache hit rate and backend thundering. 500s on kv-store. Preemptively disabling prefetch?
jonas: yup i see it in dashboards too. hit-rate for prefix cache down from ~78% to ~6% within minutes of deploy. backend QPS spiked x8.
alyssa: logs look like cache key mismatch flood, many keys flagged as 'miss:canonicalization':
```
2026-03-18T09:12:05Z WARN cache.lookup miss key="pfx:uid:1234:tok_split:0xdeadbeef" reason=canonicalization_mismatch
2026-03-18T09:12:05Z WARN service.kv request_id=abc123 status=503 err="connection queue overflow"
```
sam: @jonas which change touched tokenizer/canonicalization?
jonas: rolled tokenizer canonicalization normalizer in last release — it changed how punctuation spacing is collapsed and added a stable-nfd normalization step. meant to reduce duplicate keys, but looks like it changed existing key format.
maya: that would explain the sudden valley — older cache entries indexed with old normalization so new lookups miss. but why the surge? prefetch warmed prefixes with new keys at high QPS so we basically flooded kv on misses.
ops-oncall: infra alerts triggered: redis pool maxclients hit, write latency 200-400ms, autoscaling triggered but lagging.
infra-bot: incident:start id=INC-2026-0318-01 severity=sev2 services=[prefix-cache, kv-store, inference-router] owner=ops-oncall
deploy-bot: rollback requested for release 1934999900 by maya — rollback queued
alyssa: immediate mitigation options: 1) disable prefetch warmup routing 2) add compatibility layer to try old key format before new 3) throttle background warmers 4) emergency kv-proxy queue backpressure.
sam: disable prefetch in routing first — quick flip in config: `prefetch.enabled=false` on routing-prod. low-risk and immediate.
jonas: agreed. i've flipped it in canary and will flip global in 30s if canary looks stable.
maya: canary looks good. global flip done. backend QPS dropped ~60% in 45s. errors still elevated from queued requests but trending down.
alyssa: while rolling back tokenizer is an option, i want smaller blast radius fix. will prepare compatibility lookup shim that tries legacy_key() before modern_key(). sketch: 
```
// pseudo
string lookup_key(ctx) {
  string k_new = modern_normalize(ctx.prompt);
  try hit = kv.get(k_new);
  if (hit) return hit;
  string k_old = legacy_normalize(ctx.prompt);
  return kv.get(k_old);
}
```
jonas: nice. we should also add a histogram metric for fallback-hit to measure legacy key utilization.
sam: created a quick canary patch for the shim on router edge, will roll to 10% and monitor.
infra-bot: deployment: canary router-shim v1935000001 -> 10% traffic
maya: perf note: fallback adds an extra kv roundtrip for misses, increases p99 latency. for hot prefixes we want to avoid that. consider a background reconcile job that reindexes legacy entries to new keys during low traffic windows.
alyssa: yes — reconcile worker plan: read prefix namespace, compute modern key, write if not present; rate-limited and paxos-safe. can run in batches and mark progress.
jonas: also, in profiling earlier this week we saw kernel fallback behavior interacting with batching: when latency jumps due to extra kv lookups our batching heuristic increases batch size to amortize kernel setup cost which actually worsens latency tail. we should clamp the batching heuristic when cache-miss-rate > 20%.
sam: good catch. i'll add a short-circuit: if prefix_miss_rate > 0.2 then use conservative_batch_policy (max_batch=8, prefer_low_latency=true).
ops-oncall: after config flips and shim canary we still had a small aftershock — kv-proxy queue drained by 02:10 UTC. all systems nominal now. no customer-facing errors per SLO warp.
maya: postmortem action items so far: 
- revert tokenizer normalization or ship compatibility shim? (decide)
- ship reconcile worker to reindex legacy keys (alyssa)
- add metric `cache.legacy_fallback` and dashboard (jonas)
- throttle warmers and add warmup rate limits per tenant (sam)
- change batching heuristic to observe runtime cache-miss-rate (maya + eng-runtime perf)
- run a small canary and perf test suite that simulates miss storms before future tokenizer changes (all)
alyssa: i'll open a changelist with the reconcile job and compatibility shim RFC. tagging eng-runtime and infra.
jonas: note for future: include key-version in key metadata (e.g., `pfx:v2:...`) so we can have explicit compatibility checks instead of heuristics.
maya: thanks everyone. adding timeline to incident ticket and will kick off a brief postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: incident:resolve id=INC-2026-0318-01 closed_by=maya duration=00:40:00 summary="prefetch warmup + tokenizer canonicalization mismatch caused mass cache misses -> kv overload; mitigated by disabling prefetch, canary shim, and throttling warmers"
jonas: followup: once reconcile runs we can re-enable prefetch with confidence. also propose an integration test that asserts stable hit-rate after tokenizer changes by hashing canonicalizations across versions.
sam: added a short-term ops toggle `routing.prefetch.throttle_threshold` to prevent runaway warmups until reconcile completes.
maya: final note — this incident highlighted cross-cutting interactions: key canonicalization, prefetch warmers, kv pool sizing, and dynamic batching. we should treat cache key format changes as infra-breaking and require coordinated rollout plan.
ops-oncall: thanks all — good coordination. leaving a few followup PRs in my queue.
